notes: Basic edge-list constructor (ALGO-CN-022 igraph_create). Three workloads scan the per-edge cost surface: path (single-degree vertices), star (one hub holds all incidences), and dense (K_n with quadratic |E|). The rust hot path is a max-scan over the input slice plus Graph::new + add_edges; for the path workload at n=100 we land at 2.9 µs (31× faster than python-igraph 90.0 µs, which pays a fixed Cython entry cost regardless of graph size). The Rust per-edge cost is ~15 ns at the path/star scale (1.53 ms for 99,999 edges ≈ 15.3 ns/edge) and stays sub-linear in the hub-degree case. Dense graphs narrow the gap (1.4-4.8× vs python) because the upstream C edge-array packing is already optimal — once edge count dominates over the Cython per-call overhead, the two converge. Capture: `cargo bench --bench bench_create` on Darwin/M-series release; python baseline via `.venv/bin/python -c 'import igraph as ig; t=time.perf_counter; …'`. Both report means; tolerances within criterion's reported 95% CI.
